text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

A four-person panel being all women is statistically unremarkable — planning and HR skew female, and panel composition alone carries almost no evidentiary weight. Raising it would signal grievance rather than substance and would likely harden attitudes if you apply again.

Your stronger point is the unanswered request. Director roles often weight political judgment, council relations and consultation skills above credentials, so a less-credentialled candidate winning is unsurprising — but you're entitled to know the criteria and how you scored.

Send a short, neutral follow-up to HR citing your original date and any applicable access-to-information or recruitment policy. If the feedback reveals criteria invented after shortlisting, or scoring inconsistencies, you'll then have something real.
